headline: Congress cancels a 2024 offshore drilling rule that required archaeological reports with every oil and gas plan on the Outer Continental Shelf.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) rule published on September 3, 2024. That rule required offshore oil and gas companies to include an archaeological report with every exploration or development plan. These reports identify human-made remains, such as shipwrecks, that are at least 50 years old. With the rule canceled, the older rules return, and a report is required only when a BOEM regional director has reason to believe archaeological resources may be in the lease area.

who_it_affects.group: Offshore oil and gas lessees and operators
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to submit an archaeological report with every plan, only when a BOEM regional director believes archaeological resources may be present.
The agency must bring back its earlier regulations and cannot issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: People and groups involved with underwater historical sites
who_it_affects.how: Fewer automatic surveys will be done to find shipwrecks and other older human remains in offshore lease areas before drilling plans are approved.
